content.title: Amy Madigan’s Oscar moment had everyone talking
content.text: NewsAmy Madigan accepts the award for actress in a supporting role for "Weapons" during the Oscars on Sunday, March 15, 2026, at the Dolby Theatre in Los Angeles. (AP Photo/Chris Pizzello)Chris Pizzello/Invision/APLOS ANGELES — Amy Madigan captured the first Oscar of the night at the 98th Annual Academy Awards, taking home the award for Best Supporting Actress for her role as the unforgettable Aunt Gladys in “Weapons.”Last year’s supporting actress winner, Zoe Saldaña, was on hand to announce the next inductee into the category’s storied history. When her name was called, Madigan made her way to the stage to a standing ovation.“This is great!” Madigan said, opening her acceptance speech with a joyous cackle. “Everybody’s asking, ‘Well, it’s been 40 years (since your first nomination). What’s different this time?’ What’s different is this gold guy.”Madigan thanked her husband, actor Ed Harris, who has supported her throughout her career. “None of it would mean anything if he wasn’t by my side,” she said. She also gave a shout-out to her dogs, drawing laughter from the audience.Madigan’s portrayal of Aunt Gladys, a chaotic and eccentric figure in “Weapons,” was widely praised by critics and audiences alike, cementing her status as a scene-stealing presence in a film already noted for its ensemble performances.RELATED: What to look for at the 2026 Oscars this eveningRELATED: Who’s presenting at tonight’s 98th Academy Awards?RELATED: Why Nicole Kidman’s Oscar day starts in a surprising placeThe win marks a milestone in Madigan’s career, coming decades after her first Academy Award nomination for “Twice in a Lifetime” in 1986.
